content:
Since iOS 5 in 2011, iPhones and iPads have included Notification Center, allowing users to view notifications from various apps in chronological order in one place.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple has made significant changes to how users access Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 is still in beta, and the first two versions operated slightly differently. However, as of the sixth developer beta, it appears this change will officially launch this fall—though I personally would prefer adjustments.

Siri AI now occupies most swipe gestures along the top edge of iPhone and iPad

By default, iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 haven't changed how Notification Center is accessed. However, enabling Siri AI changes one key swipe gesture on iPhone and iPad.

When Siri AI is enabled, one way to summon Siri is by swiping down from the middle of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad screen. This gesture was previously used to open Notification Center.

Even with Siri AI enabled, you can still swipe down from the top-left corner to open Notification Center. Notifications now slide in from the top-left corner as a way to signal that the touch-accessible area for Notification Center has shrunk.

Apple has heavily prioritized user access to Siri AI in iOS 27, with most of the top edge reserved for summoning this new Siri experience.

The last time Apple changed how Notification Center is accessed was with the iPhone X launch, when Control Center was moved from swiping up from the bottom to swiping down from the top-right. Apple later standardized this experience across devices.

Notifications have now been pushed to the top-left corner

Now it's Notification Center's turn to be pushed into a corner. Particularly in iPadOS 27 beta 1, the area above home screen app icons is almost entirely reserved for Siri AI activation. If you turn off the AM/PM or date display, the area for opening Notification Center effectively shrinks further.

Top Liked Comment by mz4srmsr

I've always swiped from the top-left to check notifications, didn't even know you could swipe from the middle 😂 Guess I'll be fine?

Apple made improvements in iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating more uniform zones on the left and right sides. The width is about two app columns—Notification Center on the left, Control Center on the right, and the rest for Siri activation.

After 15 years of muscle memory, it'll take some time to decide whether this change is worth it. In the meantime, early reactions to Apple's new Siri AI system have been generally quite positive. Hearing "Siri is finally useful now," I think we all need time to adjust.

After months of using this new operation, I can confidently say I'd turn it off if there were an option. Since there's currently no setting to disable the swipe-down-from-top-center gesture for Siri, the only option is to build new muscle memory and deliberately avoid the center area.

iOS 27 is currently available as developer and public beta, with an expected official release next month.
